issues.legal_issue: A later enhancement award or appellate judgment does not revive the time to seek redetermination when the earliest qualifying enhancement award preceded the commencement of the redetermination scheme.
material_facts: The claimants accepted the Collector’s compensation without protest and did not seek a reference.
The earliest award enhancing compensation on a reference was made before the redetermination scheme came into force.
A later appellate judgment enhanced compensation, and a further reference award was made after the scheme came into force.
The claimants relied on those later decisions in seeking redetermination.
issues.conclusion: The later award and appellate judgment did not provide a fresh cause of action or limitation period. The claimants could not obtain redetermination on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 28-A(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, the application must be made within three months of the earliest qualifying award by a civil court on a reference under section 18; later awards and appellate judgments do not revive an expired right or create a fresh cause of action. The provision operates prospectively from September 24, 1984. The Court applied Babua Ram v. State of U.P., [1994] Supp 4 SCR 148, and Scheduled Castes Co-operative Land Owning Society, Bhatinda v. Union of India, [1991] 2 SCC 174.

rule.if: redetermination_proceeding and claimant_did_not_seek_reference and earliest_enhancement_award_predated_scheme and later_enhancement_decisions_followed

predicates.redetermination_proceeding: The proceeding seeks redetermination of compensation for acquired land by a claimant who did not obtain a reference.
predicates.claimant_did_not_seek_reference: The claimant accepted the original compensation without protest and did not seek a reference.
predicates.earliest_enhancement_award_predated_sche: The earliest award enhancing compensation on a reference was made before the redetermination scheme came into force.
predicates.later_enhancement_decisions_followed: One or more later reference awards or appellate decisions enhanced compensation after the earliest award.

issues.definition: When a claimant who did not seek a reference relies on later enhancement decisions, an earliest enhancement award that predates the scheme means those later decisions do not create a fresh redetermination right.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot obtain parity in enhanced compensation from other claimants when the statutory route to redetermination is unavailable.
material_facts: The claimants had accepted compensation without protest and had not sought a reference.
Other claimants obtained higher compensation through references and appeals.
The claimants argued that equality and parity entitled them to the higher compensation.
issues.conclusion: The parity argument did not entitle the claimants to increased compensation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the parity and Article 14 argument had been considered and rejected in Babua Ram v. State of U.P., [1994] Supp 4 SCR 148, and rejected it for the same reasons in this case.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compensation for acquired land.
predicates.claimant_did_not_seek_reference: The claimant accepted the original compensation without protest and did not seek a reference.
predicates.earliest_enhancement_award_predated_sche: The earliest award enhancing compensation on a reference was made before the redetermination scheme came into force.
predicates.other_claimants_received_higher_compensa: Other claimants whose land was acquired under the same notification obtained higher compensation.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition compensation proceeding, a claimant who did not seek a reference cannot obtain increased compensation solely because other claimants received more when the earliest enhancement award predates the scheme.

issues.legal_issue: Statutory additions to compensation are not an independent entitlement, and a court cannot award them when the underlying redetermination award was made without jurisdiction.
material_facts: The Collector made a redetermination award based on later enhancement decisions even though the earliest qualifying enhancement award predated the redetermination scheme.
The Collector did not include statutory additions to compensation.
The claimants sought those additions in a writ petition, and the High Court directed that they be awarded.
The underlying redetermination award was without jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The Collector’s redetermination award was a nullity, and neither the Collector nor the High Court could award statutory additions independently of a valid enhancement of compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 28-A(3), 18 to 28, 23(1), 23(1-A), and 28 of the Land Acquisition Act provide for statutory additions in connection with a court’s determination of compensation exceeding the Collector’s section 11 award; they do not create an independent power to award those additions. Because the Collector lacked jurisdiction to make the underlying redetermination, the High Court also erred in granting the additions.

predicates.land_acquisition_redetermination_proceed: The proceeding concerns redetermination of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.underlying_redetermination_lacked_jurisd: The Collector based the redetermination on enhancement decisions that did not provide a valid basis for reopening the original compensation award.
predicates.statutory_additions_sought_without_valid: The claimant sought statutory additions without a valid court determination enhancing compensation above the original award.

issues.definition: When a redetermination proceeding rests on an invalid reopening and no valid court enhancement supports the additions, statutory additions cannot be awarded independently.
